searchText: i would argue a full node doesn't really need to serve the second bullet here - "full" node ideally means participating in consensus or following the chain with a rolling world state (but not every world state, like an archive node). old blocks, yes - as full nodes store the entire chain and needs to serve segments of it to their peers (or some section of it, as Besu and nethermind have options to drop some histroy today, using checkpointing). Oh interesting — - what is the status quo right now wrt requesting rpc data about historical transactions? - does this imply that some besu and nethermind nodes will just say “we don’t have this block” if they’ve dropped the history and it is being requested by some peer? Last question seems off because if all we had were besu and nethermind nodes, then history would eventually get lost and or it would become hard/impossible to sync from genesis
